name: Lionel Wu
life: “I still remember scoring a domino match on the back of a payslip.” People around the downtown fountain know Lionel by a small Thursday habit. Lionel keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I beat them at dominoes as a teenager. I want one last game with both clocks still ticking on company time.
appearance: Lionel has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a straight nose and deep-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Lionel touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Lionel treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Lionel lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To play the last scored game before clocking out.
family: Lydia Ames is Lionel’s stepsibling. A relative let everybody believe a favorite tune was a folk song. Only later did the family find the melody in a book with a relative's real name under it. Lionel wants the person who made something to have a chance to claim it. Asked about *The pawned trumpet*, Lydia says, “I sold the trumpet with a practice mute. The mute is still on my shelf and so is the child's name.”
connections: Joel Arendt. Packed lunches and one last scorecard complicate the story that only two people are retiring.

reactions.situation: A younger worker is asked to perform the final lift
reactions.response: Lionel lets the trainee carry out the job they are qualified for and keeps space for the retirees to watch.
reactions.asWritten: A younger worker is asked to perform the final lift. Lionel lets the trainee carry out the job they are qualified for and keeps space for the retirees to watch.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Lionel asks the person crying whether they want to go somewhere quieter, leaving them control over the next step.
reactions.asWritten: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face. Lionel asks the person crying whether they want to go somewhere quieter, leaving them control over the next step.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Lionel says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
